submission.justification: Algorithm-L1 with a threshold of 34 GeV achieves the highest signal efficiency of 92.99% at the allocated 8 kHz rate, significantly outperforming Algorithm-L2 (87.23% at 35 GeV) and Algorithm-L3 (74.39% at 30 GeV). This recommendation directly addresses the primary goal of achieving the highest possible signal efficiency. The iterative topological clustering with learned calibration provides superior performance by better reconstructing the signal topology. The 34 GeV threshold is well within the required 20-60 GeV range and represents the optimal operating point that balances signal acceptance against the rate constraint. All three candidate algorithms were stated to fit within FPGA resource budgets, and since Algorithm-L1 is listed as a viable candidate, it is expected to meet the 4.0 μs latency requirement from front-end buffer constraints.

Algorithm-L1's iterative nature may have higher latency than simpler algorithms, but its inclusion as a candidate implies it meets this hard requirement.
